probes.question: Which client code path issues GET /grants, and under what precondition?
probes.method: Read-only. `grep -rn "/grants" src/ e2e/` for callers, then read of the caller and its mount site.
findings: EXACTLY ONE browser-side caller exists: `fetchGrants` at src/components/campaign/share/CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:62-83, issuing `fetch('/api/campaigns/<id>/grants')` at :66-69. (e2e/campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts:329 is a test-side APIRequestContext call, not a browser call.)

Its precondition is `isSource` -- src/components/campaign/share/CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:103 `const isSource = authority !== null && authority.role === 'source'`, enforced in `load` at :105-111 (`if (!isSource) { setGrants([]); return; }`). The fetch is therefore PROOF that the browser read authority.role === 'source'.

Mount site: src/components/gameplay/pages/campaigns/dashboard/CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:365-368 renders `<CampaignSharePanelConnected campaignId={campaign.id} matchId={getCoopMatchId(campaign.coopSession)} />` UNCONDITIONALLY on the campaign dashboard -- for the host AND for the guest.

The component's own header comment at :16-18 states the intended contract: 'Grants are fetched only for a source. A replica may not list them and the server would refuse, so asking would be a guaranteed-failed request whose answer the panel already knows.' It mirrors only the FIRST of the route's two gates.
probes.verdict: Caller identified. The client's precondition is a property of the CAMPAIGN (is it a source), not of the CALLER.

probes.question: Is the guest's call legitimate for its role? (spec question)
probes.method: Read of the route's cited spec and of the two gate implementations.
citations: openspec/changes/design-campaign-authority-and-sync/specs/campaign-replication/spec.md:5-10 -- 'Requirement: Sharing issues grants; grants create replicas that know their provenance'. The SHALLs assign issuing and listing to the SOURCE: '...and the source SHALL list all three active grants'. No SHALL anywhere in campaign-replication grants a guest, grantee or replica the capability to LIST a campaign's grants.

src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/grants.ts:8-19 (header) -- the two gates are documented as answering different questions: `not-source` is a property of the CAMPAIGN ('Every browser this server serves reads the same answer, co-op guests included, so it authorizes nobody on its own'); `not-campaign-gm` is a property of the CALLER ('Sharing is the GM's administration surface').

src/lib/campaign/grants/campaignShareService.ts:177-188 -- listShareGrants checks requireSourceCampaign FIRST, then requireCampaignGm, so a `not-campaign-gm` answer PROVES the campaign passed the source gate.

src/lib/campaign/grants/campaignShareService.ts:103-135 -- requireCampaignGm returns ok when the campaign has no active seat (the #33 / #29 boundary), refuses when the caller is empty or is not the active gm seat. A `not-campaign-gm` 403 therefore also proves the campaign HAS an active seat and the caller presented a VALID token (an invalid/absent token on a seated campaign is 401 at grants.ts:129-132, and zero 401s were observed).
probes.verdict: The guest's call is NOT legitimate. The server gate is correct and spec-aligned; listing grants is the GM's administration surface. The defect is that the client asks.

rootCause.statement: The co-op GUEST browser's campaign dashboard mounts the GM-only share panel, whose fetch precondition mirrors only the FIRST of the grants route's two authorization gates. On a shared-server co-op session both browsers read the SAME campaign record, whose stored D2 authority is `source`, so the guest's panel satisfies `isSource` and issues GET /api/campaigns/<id>/grants. The server passes the source gate and then refuses on the CALLER gate -- `not-campaign-gm` -- because the guest holds a grantee seat, not the campaign's active `gm` seat. Chromium surfaces each refusal as a console error, and the audit spec's blanket sweep at e2e/coop-campaign-ui-audit.spec.ts:843 has no allowance for it.
chain: CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:365-368 mounts CampaignSharePanelConnected unconditionally, for host and guest alike.

CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:103 computes isSource from the STORED campaign authority -- a property of the campaign, identical for every browser this server serves (grants.ts:11-14 says so verbatim).
CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:105-111 gates the fetch on isSource alone, so the guest fetches.
campaignShareService.ts:182-185 passes the source gate, then refuses at requireCampaignGm -> reason 'not-campaign-gm'.
grants.ts:68 maps that refusal to 403; grants.ts:140-145 sends it.

attachErrorCapture (spec:195-215) records the browser's resource-error console line; its critical() filter (spec:207-213) excludes only Hydration/HMR/Fast Refresh/favicon/^net::/ResizeObserver/legacyBehavior/codemod, so a 403 survives.
The terminal assertion at spec:843 fails with exactly 4 entries -- one per guest dashboard mount.

classification.verdict: PRODUCT DEFECT -- the client calls an endpoint its role cannot access.
classification.notTestExpectation: The audit spec's sweep is doing its job. A 403 that a shipped client provokes on a normal, supported user path IS a defect signal, and the spec has not changed since #1053. Adding an allowance would hide a live client/server contract mismatch rather than fix it.
classification.notEnvironment: The refusal is produced by an application authorization branch (campaignShareService.ts:131-133) reached identically in either server mode; its inputs (the SQLite campaign row, the participant seat table, the caller's bearer) are supplied by playwright.config.ts webServer.env in both. No port, timeout, dependency or harness-contract fault is involved; zero 401s and zero not-source refusals were observed.
classification.notTheGate: The server gate is CORRECT and spec-aligned (P2). #1521 closed a real exposure -- before it, any client that knew a campaign id could read every grantee's principal id and revoke another player's access. The fix must not weaken it.
classification.ownership: NOT owned by camp-01b, camp-01c or camp-01d. No wave's frozen assertion set references grants, sharing or console hygiene, and all three waves' own assertions converted to their expected values. The grants route and the share panel belong to design-campaign-authority-and-sync (campaign-replication).
classification.topologyScope: Measured on the shared-server co-op topology the journey exercises (both browsers, one server, one campaign record). On a two-device topology the guest's device holds a REPLICA, authority.role is 'replica', and the existing isSource guard already suppresses the call. UNVERIFIED by this lane: the two-device path was not run.

minimalCorrectFix.principle: Restore the invariant the component already claims (CampaignSharePanelConnected.tsx:16-18, 'asking would be a guaranteed-failed request whose answer the panel already knows') and that the presentational panel states as a rule (CampaignSharePanel.tsx:12-16, 'showing a control that always fails is its own kind of lie'). The client must not ask for the GM's administration surface unless it can be the GM.
minimalCorrectFix.theFactTheClientAlreadyHas: `campaign.coopSession.mode` is exactly 'host' | 'guest' (src/types/campaign/CoopSession.ts:37 CoopSessionMode; :50-88 ICoopSession). The mount site already destructures the same object one line away -- CampaignDashboardPage.tsx:367 calls getCoopMatchId(campaign.coopSession). No new server round-trip, no new state, no inference.

change.what: Accept the local co-op role as a prop and narrow the fetch precondition from `isSource` to `isSource && coopMode !== 'guest'`. A guest mirror keeps rendering the panel from its stored authority; it simply stops issuing a request whose refusal is already known.

Correct the two stale comments, which describe only the replica case and predate the caller gate #1521 added. This is documentation of the invariant, not decoration -- the stale comment is why the second gate was never mirrored.
Pass `coopMode={campaign.coopSession?.mode}` alongside the matchId it already passes.

minimalCorrectFix.sizeEstimate: 3 files, well under 30 changed lines, plus the unit test that pins 'a guest-mode panel issues no grants request' (the behaviour that can actually break).

whyNotTheOtherShapes.weakenTheServerGate: REJECTED -- reopens the #1521 exposure and contradicts campaign-replication, which assigns listing to the source/GM.
whyNotTheOtherShapes.swallowTheClientError: REJECTED -- fetchGrants already tolerates the refusal (`if (!response.ok) return []`, :70). The console line is emitted by the BROWSER for the failed resource, not by the app, so no client-side catch can suppress it. Only not issuing the request removes it.
whyNotTheOtherShapes.filterTheSweep: REJECTED as the primary fix -- see frozenFileImpact.

ownerDecisions.question: Should a co-op GUEST's dashboard render the share panel at all?
ownerDecisions.context: On a shared server the guest's stored authority is 'source' (it is literally the host's record), so CampaignSharePanel currently renders the GM's share surface to the guest -- today with a live Revoke button beside every grant row the fetch returns. The proposed fix empties the grant list, which removes the failing request and the Revoke buttons, but still shows the guest an empty share box rather than the 'you are a guest mirror' truth.
ownerDecisions.whyNotDecidedHere: Answering it means deciding what a shared-server guest's authority SHOULD read, which is a campaign-replication design question owned by design-campaign-authority-and-sync -- beyond the 403 this lane was asked to diagnose.
